next_cycle.title: CLI: minimal viable commands (forge init, run, sessions, status, verify, evidence, checkpoint, doctor) — with --json
next_cycle.prompt: Wire the 8 minimal CLI commands under packages/forge-cli/src/commands/. Read the existing config.ts and index.ts first. Each command is a function that takes args, calls into state-store + agent-loop or returns JSON. (1) forge init — idempotent setup: write .env, init Postgres schema (calls store.init()), create .gitignore. (2) forge run <task> — invokes AgentLoop.run(task). (3) forge sessions — list tasks from state store. (4) forge status [taskId] — single task summary. (5) forge verify <taskId> — list open verification matrix. (6) forge evidence <taskId> [--claim id] — list evidence ledger. (7) forge checkpoint <taskId> — list patch candidates. (8) forge doctor — env + DB + provider reachability check. Each command MUST support --json flag for headless output. Wire them into cli.ts as subcommands. CRITICAL: capture exit code correctly — pnpm -r build > /tmp/build.log 2>&1; echo $? (do NOT pipe through tail). Tests at tests/cli-commands.test.ts: each command tested with --json and --text output. 20-minute budget. Report commit hash.
next_cycle.verify_prompt: 1. STEP ZERO: pnpm -r clean && pnpm -r build > /tmp/build.log 2>&1; echo "exit=$?". FAIL hard if exit != 0 OR if the log contains 'error TS' or 'Failed'. Catches the workspace-level tsbuildinfo staleness that bit us twice. 2. pnpm test green (must include new tests/cli-commands.test.ts). 3. Run each of the 8 commands with --json: forge init, forge sessions, forge status, forge verify, forge evidence, forge checkpoint, forge doctor. Assert exit 0 AND stdout is parseable JSON. 4. The --text variants must also work (assert exit 0, no JSON parse exception). 5. Open cli.ts and confirm all 8 are wired as subcommands (not just exported). 6. Adversarial: forge evidence --claim nonexistent — assert non-zero exit + error message, not a silent empty list.
